title: 第二章 沙漠孤舟
content_zh:
不知过了多久，陈默在一阵剧烈的咳嗽中醒来。

    喉咙像被砂纸磨过，火辣辣地疼。他挣扎着推开变形的驾驶舱门，热浪夹杂着沙尘扑面而来，呛得他又是一阵猛咳。客舱里一片死寂，乘客们横七竖八地歪在座位上，双目紧闭，呼吸微弱——像是集体陷入了沉睡。

    “有人吗？”陈默的声音嘶哑得几乎听不见。他踉跄着穿过过道，摸了摸前排一位老人的脉搏，还算平稳，悬着的心稍稍放下。机身左侧的应急出口已经变形，他用消防斧砸了十几下，才勉强撬开一条缝。

    钻出去的瞬间，陈默倒吸一口凉气。

    飞机斜插在一片无垠的沙漠里，机翼折断了一侧，机身布满划痕，像一头搁浅的钢铁巨兽。四周是连绵起伏的沙丘，金红色的沙粒在烈日下泛着刺眼的光，看不到半点植被，更别说人烟。天空是纯粹的蓝，没有一丝云，只有太阳像个烧红的烙铁，悬在头顶。

    “通讯器？”他摸向腰间，对讲机早已没了信号。他爬上机顶，拿出应急信号发射器，连续按了十几下，屏幕上只有“无信号”三个字在闪烁。

    太阳渐渐西斜，沙漠的温度骤降。陈默回到客舱，给几位呼吸较弱的乘客盖了毯子，又检查了应急物资——只剩下三瓶水和半袋压缩饼干。他知道不能等，必须尽快找到水源和人烟。

    “等我回来。”他对着沉睡的乘客们低声说，像是承诺，又像是给自己打气。他带上一瓶水、半包饼干和一把瑞士军刀，锁好舱门，朝着太阳落下的方向走去。

    沙丘像凝固的波浪，一眼望不到头。走了不到两个小时，水就见了底。喉咙干得发疼，每走一步都像踩在棉花上。他开始出现幻觉，看到远处有绿洲，跑过去却只有更多的沙子。

    不知走了多久，天边泛起鱼肚白。就在他快要倒下时，眼角突然瞥见一抹不一样的颜色——不是金色的沙，是土黄色的墙。

    他揉了揉眼睛，没错，是一片低矮的房屋，像蘑菇一样散落在不远处的平地上。房屋周围有栅栏，里面似乎还有人影在晃动。

    陈默用尽最后一丝力气跑过去，在距离村庄几十米的地方，腿一软，栽倒在沙地里。意识模糊的最后一刻，他听到了说话声，不是他熟悉的任何一种语言，却带着一种古老而粗糙的质感。
content_en:
I don't know how long it took, but Chen Mo woke up with a violent cough.

    My throat felt like it had been rubbed with sandpaper, and it hurt. He struggled to push open the deformed cockpit door, and heat waves mixed with sand and dust hit his face, choking him and coughing violently again. There was a dead silence in the cabin. The passengers were slumped in their seats, with their eyes closed and their breathing weak - as if they had collectively fallen into a deep sleep.

    "Is there anyone?" Chen Mo's voice was so hoarse that it was almost inaudible. He staggered across the aisle and felt the pulse of an old man in the front row. It was still stable, and his hanging heart was slightly relieved. The emergency exit on the left side of the fuselage was deformed. He hit it with a fire ax more than a dozen times before he could barely pry it open.

    The moment he got out, Chen Mo took a breath of cold air.

    The plane was stuck diagonally in an endless desert, with one wing broken off and the fuselage covered with scratches, like a stranded steel giant. Surrounded by rolling sand dunes, the golden-red sand gleams dazzlingly under the scorching sun. There is no vegetation at all, let alone human habitation. The sky is pure blue, without a trace of cloud, and only the sun hangs overhead like a red-hot iron.

    "Communicator?" He touched his waist, but the walkie-talkie had already lost its signal. He climbed up to the top of the machine, took out the emergency signal transmitter, and pressed it a dozen times in succession. Only the words "No signal" flashed on the screen.

    The sun gradually sets in the west, and the temperature of the desert drops sharply. Chen Mo returned to the cabin, covered several passengers with weak breathing with blankets, and checked the emergency supplies - only three bottles of water and half a bag of compressed biscuits were left. He knew he couldn't wait, he had to find water and human habitation as soon as possible.

    "Wait until I come back." He whispered to the sleeping passengers, like a promise and a pep talk to himself. He took a bottle of water, half a pack of biscuits and a Swiss Army knife, locked the cabin door, and walked towards the setting sun.

    The sand dunes are like solid waves, endless as far as the eye can see. After walking for less than two hours, the water bottomed out. My throat was so dry that it hurt, and every step I took felt like I was stepping on cotton. He began to hallucinate, seeing an oasis in the distance, only to find more sand when he ran towards it.

    I don’t know how long I walked, but the sky turned white. Just when he was about to fall, he suddenly caught a glimpse of a different color from the corner of his eye - not golden sand, but an earthy yellow wall.

    He rubbed his eyes. Yes, it was a cluster of low houses, scattered like mushrooms on the flat land not far away. There was a fence around the house, and there seemed to be figures moving inside.

    Chen Mo ran over with the last of his strength. A few dozen meters away from the village, his legs gave out and he fell down in the sand. At the last moment of his confusion, he heard voices, not in any language he was familiar with, but with an ancient and rough texture.
